subject: VPC upgrade: surge-control procedures, evacuation scripts, and AAR
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@mountaindb.com>, Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@mountaindb.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC upgrade: surge-control procedures, evacuation scripts, and AAR

Hi Alex / Rita —

Following our site-readiness call last week, we're scheduling the VPC maintenance for your private deployment on 2025-07-08 UTC window (03:00–05:00 UTC). This thread captures the operational plan, surge-control knobs, and the evacuation script we'll use if we need to unpin traffic from the upgrade cohort.

Primary asks for MountainDB: please confirm whether you want the canary cohort limited to 5% or we should default to automatic ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with 30-minute health checks. Also confirm that your networking team can accept a temporary IP-mapping change if we do an emergency backout.

I've attached the checklist and a stripped-down evacuation script for the runbook. Key bullets:
- Version pin: target runtime 2.14.0 → roll in 3 phases (canary, mid, fleet)
- Surge-control: token-based drain + 200ms per-token soft limit on canary
- Abort criteria: 10% 1-min error spike OR sustained tail-latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive checks
- Rollback: automated unshelve to previous pin + network-level traffic re-route script (evacuation-script.sh.txt)

Karthik / Grace — please review the abort criteria and confirm we have circuit-breaker telemetry wired into the shiproom dashboard. Marissa, can you own post-run AAR and ensure the postmortem template is ready?

Thanks,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): vpc-upgrade-checklist-v1.2.pdf; evacuation-script.sh.txt

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@mountaindb.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@mountaindb.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: surge-control procedures, evacuation scripts, and AAR

Thanks, Irene.

We prefer an explicitly limited canary (5% fixed) for the first two weeks post-upgrade. The automatic ramp is fine only if we see no degradations after 48 hours — otherwise keep it locked at 5% and manual promote. Also confirming networking can accept temporary IP mapping change; I'll loop in our infra lead if needed.

A couple of clarifying questions:
- Can the evacuation script perform a weighted 100% drain (move 100% off cluster A -> cluster B) without a rolling-deploy on the client side?
- For the abort criteria, can we add a secondary check for model-quality regressions on a small labeled prompt set (we have a 1k prompt smoke-check) to avoid silent quality drops?

Alex
Ops Lead, MountainDB
Attachment(s): none

On Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 09:12 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Following our site-readiness call last week, we're scheduling...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@mountaindb.com>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: surge-control procedures, evacuation scripts, and AAR

Alex — good captures. Answers inline:

- Evacuation script: yes, it manipulates our routing layer and backend weights so we can shift 100% without a client-side deploy. The script pushes the traffic to a warm standby fleet and flips the BGP/route-map entries (we coordinate with your edge).

- Model-quality smoke: absolutely agree. Add a model-quality gate: run the 1k prompt set after the canary window; if any metric (exact-match or top-1 sanity check) drops > 1.5% relative to baseline, trigger abort. We'll add the hook that pulls MountainDB's labeled set from the secure GCS path you provide.

Operational notes:
- Circuit-breaker telemetry: Grace, can you confirm the shiproom shows the per-pin CB stats? We want an alert that surfaces 10% error spike AND an ops-owner ack within 5 mins, otherwise auto-evac.
- Runbook patch sequence: preflight (health, KV warmup) -> pin apply -> canary -> 30m check -> mid-roll -> 30m check -> fleet-roll -> 1h stability window.

I'll attach the ramp script and a small YAML that encodes abort thresholds.

-k

Attachment(s): vpc-ramp-config.yaml

From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@mountaindb.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 08:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: surge-control procedures, evacuation scripts, and AAR

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple operational clarifications from our infra team:
- The warm standby has capacity for 70% of peak; if we push 100% onto standby during an evacuation we may see degraded tail latencies on their side. What's the recommended fallback if the standby becomes overloaded?
- We run internal security scans during maintenance windows. Will the pin change / image pull cause additional ephemeral IPs that need to be whitelisted?

For the model-quality gate we'll provide read-only access to the labeled set via a signed URL; please coordinate with our security contact (secops@mountaindb.com).

Thanks, Rita
Senior SRE, MountainDB

From: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@mountaindb.com>, Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@mountaindb.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 10:14:07 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC upgrade: surge-control procedures, evacuation scripts, and AAR

Rita — great questions. Short answers:

- Standby overload: the evacuation script has an early-warning step that queries standby capacity via telemetry and will cap the shift to 80% if observed available CPU/mem drops below a safety threshold. If standby is overloaded, we do a hybrid maneuver: route 60% to standby and 40% to a cold spillover pool with stricter rate limits and request-sampling enabled (this preserves throughput while protecting tail latencies). The runbook documents this decision tree and the guardrails.

- Ephemeral IPs: image pulls may originate from our build/bastion pool during the preflight; we provide a short-lived list of IP ranges in the checklist. If your security scans require whitelisting, those ranges are included in vpc-upgrade-checklist-v1.2.pdf. We can also provide S3/GCS signed-read endpoints to avoid wide IP exceptions.

I'll also confirm CB visibility in the shiproom and add the model-quality gate to the health checks pipeline.

Grace
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
